applicability.reason: Held, with the blocker RE-MEASURED and NARROWED rather than carried forward. The earlier reason was that no compaction or controlled compaction hook existed anywhere in the runtime. Two of the three pieces now exist and are tested: the heap stores objects in relocatable slots, `RuntimeHeap::compact` really moves them (a unit test frees earlier slots and asserts an object changes slot while its identity hash is unchanged), and `NativeFixture.compact_gc` exposes a controlled compaction point that answers how many objects MOVED and exposes no address, as this row requires. What is still missing is REACHABILITY: there is no root set, mark, or sweep, and the evaluator never frees a heap object, so from Iris source nothing can become dead and `compact_gc` was measured returning 0 every time - after a dead binding in a scoped block and after a loop allocating five instances. Wiring the row on that would make its central claim - that the hash is unchanged ACROSS MOVEMENT - vacuously true, since no movement would have occurred. D-111 ties the guarantee specifically to movement by GC, so the row stays held until a tracing collector can make an unreachable object's slot free.

expect.status: Same runtime-local hash in 0..2^64-1; fixture exposes no address.
